title: A Sisyphean Life (except there’s you)
subtitle: Dearest Atlas,
html:
Dearest Atlas,

It’s been a while since I have spoken to you; well – atleast in so many words. Last time I took huffs as breaths in the confused stiffness I felt as life, and sent my regards through windborne letters. Did you end up catching them?

At any rate, its night again, a chilly spacious one at that, and I scratch my pen against this page to keep it warm. It seems to be working. Don’t worry; I rest my back against the old ball. I’ve decided to call it Fred. After fred astaire. Don’t ask me; why you know I don’t think about these things.

Tonight again, my thoughts get back to you. So, let’s talk about you. You – the mastermind, carrying the weight of your sky. Does it get inside your head too, and call itself your life? Does it say unkind things to you in the silence of the night?. I’ve heard that the wind gets particularly chilly this time around. I wish I could keep your ears warm, but you know. Someday me and Fred will come visit you. I promise then, to be the company to your misery.

You know, I always thought that I could do it all. Be every Greek legend, and talk to every woeful stranger. Add the weight of the world as a dazzling outfit on Fred. But lately it feels like the mist is clearing out slowly. I can see the ridges on fred, that I never saw before. Well, i wish i could show you, if you do wanna see them.

I often wonder what your sky looks like. You don’t really talk about it, and well, you’re plenty more interesting around it. I am too, usually, you just caught me on a bad day. I wonder naively what days are hard and easy for you. I wonder whether its the rain that keep you shivering, or the sunny days that you must live past. The few times we met, I watched you so closely; that I feel like I could know the world you call your own. Is the sky beautiful? Do you want to rest your weary head?

I get a little ashamed of these ideas. But it’s alright, I am used to Fred. and in a way I stay moving. Or something. I, admit, for the first time in so long – I don’t really know what I’m doing. I just wish I could talk to you again. Your hair gray in familiar ways. Those eyes that held the world together. Hey friend, do you reckon it would be easier, if we did it all sometime together?

Goodnight.I slipped a little. I await to see you, under the sky of stars.

Yours; perhaps happily,

Sisyphus

title: checkpoint, oct 2026
subtitle: to all the things that stuck.
html:
I learnt a lot this month. This article is a personal checkpoint, but I am writing it here, because I write here when it feels true. Here is to Oct 1st - Oct 20th.

  1. Living away from my university campus has given me access to consistent, rich, deeply enmeshed, female friendships. There is so much reciprocity in how much we care for each other. I always had such female friendships, but this is the first time they are such a huge part of my day. I learnt that you can be everything, smart, beautiful, driven, loving, happy, real — and so much more. These girls inspire me everyday, and I feel like finally after a while, I’m learning to live completely honestly. I find myself taking the leap to be fully myself more — it shows up in little leaps in everyday things — like discussing my career goals, or dressing up when I’m not fully confident, talking about things I’m passionate about (work, stupid ruminations, delusionships all of that). It feels like I am finding my voice again. Its now a bodily truth that I must!must!must! cultivate my female friendships so much more.

  2. I learnt that I do not need to find a local minima in one kind of identity. I like writing, I like old art, and all of that — in a clustering algorithm — would point to one kind of person. I find myself watching a lot more crime / noir movies, and reading philosophy, and watching videos & reels about sales and business, and being hella passionate about math. I used to think that these all things need to come together into some unified form of self that I needed to present in conversation. I would hypertune the parts of me that aligned to certain people, and if I found someone to be inspiring, I’d dial up that version of me more. But I am learning to random sample different hobbies, and pay attention to the things that I actually like and find interesting. I also think, its okay that I don’t find somethings fun and interesting; while others may find it so. I don’t know if this is a very obvious thing for people to understand. The learning from this is that 1, you do not need to be completely known by people, and ironically the self is not something that you need to sell, when the selfhood that you try to compress into, isn’t authentic to you. Its better to just live, and whatever version of you that comes out is a better window into you. I felt this very deeply today, when my roommate told me she missed me (<3). It came to me all of a sudden, that I didn’t try to be anyone with her, and she, somehow cares for me anyway; and it was completely separate, and organically different from how I really care for her.

  3. To think, to wait, to fast. I learnt this from siddhartha (herman hesse), and my interpretation of this is different. To think is to be the observer of your life, to make connections in a way that is intentional. To wait is to put in effort at things, despite it not resulting in something right now — to put off impulsive pursuits; to look at habits I’m building and have faith for them despite non-immediate pay offs. I look at fasting, not as traditional fasting, rather as ways of restricting desire. This again ties to instant gratification. This can show up in me deciding to run slowly instead of fast (in order to not re injure myself), not pick at my skin, and more.

  4. How to talk to people. I think its important to give space and ask intentionally good questions. Siddhartha (the book) showed me that its importance to set intentional energy to be patient in conversation; and listen to another.

  5. Similar to the previous point, clarity comes only when you are quiet. It, also, takes a certain amount of comfort with yourself to allow & accept what feels true to you.

  6. I read Olive Kitteridge (Elizabeth Strout) which showed me the wholeness of a human being. Olive, in the story is loud, brash, self aware at instances, feels herself to be this physical big (in personality, in assuredness, in size) that she holds shamefully. This is often also directed towards her, because, it is true to how she is. The book also showed me how this character is so utterly loving and lovable. I can’t say this in a lot of clear terms, but I think it shifted something in me, to try to love myself more.

  7. Breakfast at Tiffany’s reminded me to really really focus on your friends when you hang out with them, and that noone is watching you — have fun!

  8. Listening to ghazals reminded me to allow myself to feel very intense things. And slow down when it comes to love (all kinds!)

  9. Doing my research and speaking to my advisor reminded me that my ideas can mean something, and something I am passionate about can amount to something.

  10. Shelby Sapp showed me the importance of learning sales and selling, and I can now see it in every aspect of life.

  11. A friend influencer reminded me that its important to own and live by our goals, and the faith that we can do it is more important than the small and big reasons we give for why we are/aren’t doing it.

  12. Cuckfucious on substack is doing a 77 day media cleanse. It made me think intentionally about what it would be like to incorporate clarity maxxing as a practice in my day as a habit (whether it is journalling, meditating, or a media cleanse of my own).

  13. I am slowly seeing that the life I can build for myself is truly more rich, and interesting than anything I can build for the gaze of anyone.

  14. A lot of unfurling is really slow. Its important to take time with things that are important.

  15. The consequences (whether discipline, health, career) are lagging indicators of my actions from a while back. I lost a certain amount of seriousness for taking care of my health a few months back. I want to be intentional (think), be patient (wait) and fast* (restrict/discipline myself) myself in small manageable ways.

  16. Don’t try to do everything. Focus on what is possible.

  17. Its, really, okay. (i put this in, because i need to remind myself of this everytime i am being intentional. it feels very true when I say it. but i admit, it doesnt settle as much as some of the other truths. so i will say it again. It’s going to be okay.)

  18. When you are tired, you still got some juice left. Push past your ease to comfort. (This is from david goggins). if its still hard to move, then take a break.

  19. Women can do it all. This comes from watching female creators and really observing how passionate they are, how much they have built and more. It also comes from me realising that the goal of my life is not finding someone to validate me through the gaze (trademarked) I have internalized all my life. It can truly be so much bigger than that.

the crux of all these separate learnings is to come to a new frame of mind — to decentre surveillance. to live in freedom, and observe the self and the world.

I am not sure what the next few months are going to look like. I shall find out.

title: evenings in gurgaon
subtitle: in the dim lighting of the evening, i unwrap the healthy pollocked sandwhich.
html:
in the dim lighting of the evening, i unwrap the healthy pollocked sandwhich. It came delivered in a little bag. My eyes, ill adjusted to the view of a calm mundane house, strained from the hours i spent staring at a screen, fall upon my sandwhich. I hadn't eaten in the past 7 hours. My skin had a stiffness to it of crust that settles, when nothing but your eyes dart across a screen. My limbs had lost its languidity. I rest my left leg up on the chain, in a half squat, and grab the semblances of my sandwhich. I shove in the chips that came with it underneath the fresh bread ravenously, and let it all sit in its perfectly sized box. And then I eat like an animal. I eat as the meat drops into the box, its small cute flavoured chunks. The sauce seeps out of the bite into my hands, which collects it all in its ridges. I wipe away, i pick up the fallen chicken, and eat and eat. A meal well earned. In the lonliness of a mundane evening.

Theres a lonliness to a back hunched over food like that. A back erect at the ding of a teams message, and feet that know how to fold themselves out of a comfort and run to a desk. A mouth used to the corporate cadence of pleasant nicities and soft can you hear mes. Is my screen visible? Ive been staring at it all day. The sun has risen up and fallen down. the mosaic around my room had changed, the rays that show unique patterns of this mundane evening I neglect.

Evening? Did I say evening?

its night now. I murmur the numbers again, double checking if my numbers are copied correctly from my code to my powerpoint. My agent gives me documents to read so I can study. I dart my eyes between three screens. My flatmate remind me to switch on the light. Their soft laughter reminding me that, man, im lucky, that i atleast have that in the little breaks my eyes take. Soft features instead of harsh screen. Round smiling faces of people i enjoy.

little ways we rest.

little ways we keep moving.

the food is barely digested. I ate my lunch at 5pm. The sharp rigor with which i ate hasn't been lost on me. The food sits in me funny. My head is a little light from the hours i spent staring at a screen. My fingers are tense but nimble, a macbook will spoil you such.

There are ways we neglect ourselves, in this growth we call “worth it”. Today was a day of little self care. so I sit here, and try to compress it all. try to let it float in a way that is nimble. try to get an anxious heart to rest, and say that a day's worth is at the days end. and that, books await, and movement awaits, and happiness awaits. And that tomorrow will be kinder.

atleast, hopefully :>

title: october 9th, 2026, 00:30
subtitle: ranjish hi sahi ~ mehdi hassan.
html:
ranjish hi sahi ~ mehdi hassan. bring your cigarette. bring your self. let’s sit. listen to this with me.

.

the world carries its half hazard fullness. it rests heavily on my head.

the comfort of a house and a balcony. the discomfort of a mind and its responsibilities

there is this, loneliness. I, say, it in words. I, don’t really know, how to use words.

anymore.

there are so many things.

i don’t know how to wear a smile, my eyes are permanently creased with pleading.

there is no love to focus on, i am, hollow, in my individualism.

my jeans are too long, they skid along this floor. my kurta is crinkled, and fits different. my eyes are closing. my mouth is slightly ajar. it isn’t funny at all. there isn’t a witty story to tell. there is no crowd to amuse.

i see, in the reflection of my phone, someone probably beautiful. her eyes are the grays of depth she learnt to not focus on. her lips carry words ajar and loud of love. the winds blow away this smoke. it lodges itself in the curls of my hair. for all these words, there is an ennui about the self. i dont care! about the self.

i speak in these words, i dont really know how to use, a transliteration of love hard to describe. i translate all day into speakable language. I, really, try, with all the haphazardness of my mind, to tell a coherent story.

right now I, really, cannot.

i’ve carried this for really long. i, don’t want to speak. i just want you to understand.

i don’t want this to be a performance. i don’t want to distill this into a representation to read later.

but, i really don’t know what else to do. i want to sing. i sing, slowly, a cracked voice, sick of all the inhibitions.

the song, is enough. my writing barely adds anything, to be very honest. there is synchronicity that someone, an ancient collective, understands.

that is the solace tonight, to get up, and go back to a world of translating my love. someday, it will be there out there. someday, please tell me, you too recognize it. today, i will work again to get it out.

.

.

.

رنجش ہی سہی دل ہی دکھانے کے لیے آ
آ پھر سے مجھے چھوڑ کے جانے کے لیے آ
پہلے سے مراسم نہ سہی پھر بھی کبھی تو
رسم و رہِ دنیا ہی نبھانے کے لیے آ
کس کس کو بتائیں گے جدائی کا سبب ہم
تو مجھ سے خفا ہے تو زمانے کے لیے آ
کچھ تو مرے پندار محبت کا بھرم رکھ
تو بھی تو کبھی مجھ کو منانے کے لیے آ
اک عمر سے ہوں لذتِ گریہ سے بھی محروم
اے راحتِ جاں مجھ کو رلانے کے لیے آ
اب تک دل خوش فہم کو ہیں تجھ سے امیدیں
یہ آخری شمعیں بھی بجھانے کے لیے آ

Translation

If it is grief so be it, come to break my heart again.

Do come, if only for the act of leaving me again.

Our relationship may not be the same as before, but even if seldom.

Come to fulfill the rituals and traditions of the world.

To whom all must I explain the reason of separation.

Come, if you are displeased with me, for the sake of the world.

Respect a little the depth of my love for you.

Come someday to placate me as well.

It has been a long time I haven’t had the luxury of grieving.

My peace-of-mind please do come back if only to make me cry.

Till now my hopeful heart is keeping some expectations from you.

But at least come back to put off these last candles of hope.

.

.

source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranjish_Hi_Sahi

title: repertoire
subtitle: dinner & diatribes, hozier | thousand eyes, fka twigs
html:
I find myself outside the front door, slightly self conscious. Suddenly, my scarf feels a little itchy. The scent of familiar musk its my nose. I fiddle with my ears. I remove the dust from the welcome mat with my feet. It picks up around me. I sway it away with my hands.

I enter the house. the wind blows the dream catchers. Someone left the balcony door open. Light percolates through a creak, holding dust as it moves. Brownian motion. Brown wooden tiles. Old hearth.

I walk up to my room. the floor board creaks more. My footsteps have a thud as I duck a little to enter. I take off my scarf and hang it on the hook.

Do you remember this little room? We sat together for nights putting up the glow in the dark eyes. A guiding light when the night gets too dark. An answer to the unanswered questions. A way to live through everything. A remnant of survival love. You and I spent so much time here. You looked closely at my face, and told me that the noises I hear from the attic are things of my imagination. You whispered quietly goodnight, and closed my eyes with your kisses. You left the door slightly ajar, so that more light will flow in. I always got up and closed the door after you left. these eyes blinked at me. I am enamored by them. I perform rest. I perform love. I perform care. I perform being.

its been years. I remember the gentle way a lover of the past walked in. In the silence of this attic, I heard his tender laugh. And my laugh. they flowed through the wind. they dreamed of the moon. The window always was open, and he snuck out every night. He traced my hands slowly, as he taught me language different. He taught me how to move my body after a long frigid winter. the floor board has small burn marks, and I trace it now, with the toe that peaks out of my old socks. I remember the silent ways we spoke, the dust in the air catching the words. give. take. power. tenderness.

the beef roast downstairs beckons me and my reveries. the familiar mold of a kitchen. cheap groceries we scavenged out of clearance sections. old scents of diatribes. fear in a souffle. gluttony in a paal payasam. recipes for generations.

the walls of this house absorb the metal clangs of the sharp words. the walls of this house held an uncomfortable quiet, a space between a chess move. the ultimate gambit, you say, was to leave. there are a million dishes to tend to. a million eyes to dust off.

.

somedays I wake up and i don’t recognize this place. the warmth of whispers from yesternight has silently left the room. there’s this cold loneliness that lingers.

.

the music flows into this room. I, had, been.. talking to you. There is this love that we all dream about. But dreams are held by these eyes on my ceiling. The moon outside will always be brighter. The moon will always look me in the eye.

title: I will probably write about you
subtitle: the little big lives of the people who dare to come close
html:
hello!

you have walked into my life now. I will probably write about you. A sullen swollen eyed child that ran away from the world into her diary, writing furiously about all the things she didn’t understand. The world got smaller and smaller, till it caved into itself. a convex to a concave. the world was big again. A fairy imagination. An astral projection to other worlds.

so we are back to you. If you looked into my eyes, and said something true.

Trust me, I’ll remember it.

And I’ll probably write about you.

in all the million ways you are expansive. In all the ways your eyes quiver where the world carved a hole in your realm of possibilities. All the ways that you said fuck it anyways.

or didn’t.

the little ways you try to get out of bed. the small ways you motivate yourself.

the ways when you are in awe of someone, you can’t help but want to show them your entire world. take all that I know you say, and please hold it.

I write about you, since i see the ways our correlation peaks.

a temporal, rhythmic signal of behavior.

A repetitive pattern, that we all try to break out of.

.

I sit in a meeting, and write this in the back of my mind.

If you think you weren’t remembered, you are.

I’m sorry there’s only so much sand I can hold in my hands.

I’m sorry I left some of it to be gold on the floor.

I hope the world sees your value, and embraces you for it.

.

I only have this letter for you.

title: wanna come to my house & play?
subtitle: Let us play a game of chess.
html:
Let us play a game of chess. This house is big and cold, and I see the light through the cracks differently from child me. If I leave the window open, the wind will remind me of my dreams. If I close my eyes, these empty floors will meander into long trails. The book doesn’t replace the magnetism of a game, so do you want to come over to my house and play?

there’s this stipulation I have. each time you lose, I ask something of you, and you have got to do it. it is only fair play — you owe it to me. don’t worry though, you are in the safety of my home.

.

think about it. it takes a certain person to be down for this. are you curious enough to sit through the tension of a slow long game?

.

If I win and win, I’ll be the one who loses. But, I’d win still. there was a night somewhere, where you let go of your apprehensions, and sat in the middle of an unfurnished house, to play chess with a girl.

.

Would you care to ask good questions? Would I answer in a way that dances with the pit in my stomach?

Would our loneliness leave paint marks on each other?

.

see. I think you are getting it. It has always been a simple game. I ask you to look at your fear. would you do that for me?

.

Shah Mat. The king is down. and somehow, I have lost too.

title: The girlboss dad.
subtitle: adding random new words to our collective consciousness-vibe based taxonomy, as a suave way to say MY DAD IS REALLY COOL (we are too nonchalant to tell this to each other)
html:
We all have heard about the girl dad — a dad that is intentionally, and actively interested, supportive and empathetic to their daughter’s interests. This often shows up in reels with dads participating in lil girly things with their daughters. Hailed to show lil girls what good masculinity looks like, the girl dads have a good rep in online discourses.

But but but! I would argue that we are sleeping on a more intense, crazy, and insane variant of the girl dad; which I term as the girlboss dad, or — the girl dad, the premium version. Here, I do not mean girlboss dad in the gaslight-gatekeep-girlboss way, rather, a no bullshit mentor, get out the best potential out of my girl child way. My dad embodies this to his core, and I bet he is too nonchalant and humble to even take this praise. But I shall hail them anyway.

For starters, my dad, (or -ahem, this kind of dad) has got all the qualities of a girl dad. This archetype of father, is nothing but excessively kind to their daughters, even when they may not understand what the daughter experiences. They are supportive of their daughter’s niche interests, and participate and show active interest in everything big or small. They are supportive, and remind their daughters that they can be whoever they want to be. They push that she is capable, pretty (pretty a lot), smart, and remind her that despite the ways women are restricted (smh india), she can really be whoever she wants to be. This is the kind of dad who calls you up at night to make sure you reached home safe, but doesn’t tell you to not go out. The kinda dad who teaches you how good masculinity looks like, and what kindness looks like.

But, added to all of these genuinely good human qualities, my dad is crazy competent, and a no-bullshit, brilliant, creative & talented individual who cannot help see some pretty damn normal things in the terms of business problems. On a general basis, my dad is super supportive of the small & big things i do. But, sometimes, he is interested with an italized i. He sees the things that im ambitious and passionate about, and engages with me about it like an absolutely sarcastic stakeholder. He thinks im funny? you should do standup. He finds me talking about adhd interesting you should put out content about this in public. I bet a lot of people haven’t figured this out in this way. He likes a research idea I’m working on? now tell me how will you adapt this into the real world. how could this make profits? He likes an article I’m writing? you should write a book! He likes my brain on a particular idea? how would you extend what you formalized?

A lot of times, I have not thought about my cool niche hobbies in a way that is realistic, or in generative ways. And when that does happen, he will crack a bunch of jokes. This gets me competitive to do better, and he riffs with me until its a good idea. It has been hands down the best kind of conversation i’ve had with the family.

This goes beyond ideas, and to things like dreams, goals and ambitions. I am one to feel things deeply, not quite understand why I am uncomfortable, or don’t like something. i tend to sink in it a little, and get stuck in decision paralysis. My dad’s endless sarcasm, and competitive jabs get me to wanna push my way into clarity. This often results in me saying “im abitious about xyz”, and him pushing me on it so much, that by the end of the day, I have an excel sheet, and a ppt and a “RAAAH I SHALL SHOW YOU” attitude; with all possible details on the xyz; just so that I can get the “hmm good job (*smug smile*)” from my excessively jovial, incredibly persistent father.

More than anything, he constantly treats me like I am smart, capable, and competent, and hence urges me to follow all my insane dreams. Enabler pro max (smh).

I can see how people see this as pressurizing. To me, its reassuring to an endless degree. It has taught me that love is more than just curiosity — its curiosity that is generative. It is endless faith and interest in all the myriad of things the other person is passionate about. It’s growing together, and pushing people past the bounds of fear that they have for themselves. Its being endlessly humble, kind, and relentless about your belief in someone else. Its actively supporting your loved ones as they build a continuous, generative, creative life. It’s teaching your kid to live fully.

Furthermore, it teaches me that love is entering the world of your loved one; and interrogating it, extending it, challenging it and holding space for the ways it sucks. My dad looks at all my stupid half-baked ideas, and told me to actually think about it till the end, all the while joking about it so much, that I can never take myself too seriously. In this way, he plays the role of a goated friend, mentor and parent all at once. and well, I have found it peak enough to write an entire article.

(he probably should cut back on the excel sheets though. those are insane. )

Some other things!

(ai, tech, writing, whimsy)

  1. I just went to bangalore + hyd and thoroughly enjoyed :)

  2. I have a lot of technical + other articles in the drafts, and plan to put them out with time :p. Technical articles range from stuff like big data platforms (like how impala, hive, iceberg, etc) work, to a lot more articles on temporal reasoning, and current temporal reasoning systems. if this is something that you care about, pls do ze subscribb

  3. Also considering to do a minimal post on inductive biases, and how to think about representation, since the senior folks at my office said that i kno a lot about it

  4. Kinda (finally) went semi public with my poetry/poetic prose substack! It contains writings that come to me like reveries, and are a lot more stylistic in nature. (still don’t wanna tie these accounts for professionalism reasons, but if you are curious enough, you can probably find it :>)

  5. almost done reading intermezzo. I have SO many thoughts. May write something about it.

  6. my plants continue to grow a lot. I missed them on my travel exploits. they are in their stubborn growth spurt, shaggy long haired son era. I might need to graft them into new pots.

  7. this is a really non technical article, and well, i do wanna write these too, interspersed with the cool shtuff.

title: ordinary day
subtitle: TV girl, high writing
html:
there is this suspension in space. Huge swathes of time where it exits my consciousness that the world i imagined and stayed limerant about will never really exist. I still dont believe it. It kinda swims around my head like a fish. Conversations about you tell me you're above it all. Theres no way id know, really.

You see an intimate part of someone accidentally, in their state of stupor. How do you let go? most people are unkind in their subconscious, or selfish. I struggle to believe you don't remember you were kind! The human behaviour continues to confuse my little brain.

My future worlds, my limerant dreams tell me that youre asking me to wait for you to figure it out. Like you would want to be kind again. But you were the kindest in real life, in your honesty, and in leaving.

I wonder often if I wasnt enough, in sequences of circles. I wonder why you float instead of teather. Do you just dance? Does it not matter then who i am? Do younot feel enough? Do you not feel?

I wonder if a man in a reverie feels inadequate. I love all the millions of versions of you I conjure up in my head. It reminds me of the expansiveness of my love. It is the way I beautifully exploit this silence of the unknown. Anyways, you would never know.

You will never know how the idea of you makes me live through life in its saffron breeze. How I slow down, breathe, and feel in my being more. How the calm takes over. My tryst with silence, and the settlement of adulthood is a dance I did while holding your metaphorical hand.

Do you like the ways words sound? The twinkle teethering steps into a trance. The dogged way breathe hitches. The Spanish twist of lovers. The blood laden feet of the Scottish faes.

I saw you again recently. Words moved fast, my eyes moved away faster. Its inconceivable to believe that its teathered so much to the idea of someone. Its shameful in its audacity, and obscene in its tenacity.

But, I also, do think, I could really love you.

I can love anyone who i give intentional care to. And I have turned over your 1000 possible lives in my head forever. I could turn over more. I, actually, can love anyone. I choose to care for you.

its a little insane. Its a raging limerance. Its the worst its been in my life. I, just keep feeling deeper and deeper.

It scares me awake. It scares me to sleep. I don't want to run.

but i speak to a reverie, and distill it down to a person. The reverie is mine. The person is you.

I ask for your forgiveness. I have used your words as a way to stand straight again. And again. And again.

You probably don't remember.

the way you altered my world

On that ordinary day.

title: if nobody is watching, what is a good life?
subtitle: diary entry monthly checkin # 1
html:
Free writing here. Hi, hello.

I have made it an active mission to stay of instagram for a month. I was, before, hyperperforming in the macro and micro ways a particular version of myself. My life felt out of control, so that performance was the place I was asserting control. Even once I left, I found myself constantly anxious for the gaze of others — and the fact that i felt like everyone else had their own lives, that I probably did not know about at all. The anxiety that I am comparatively living a shitty life, or doing something which wasn’t glamorous got to me often; but since I didnt have a way to prove I was right or wrong — with time this anxiety settled down.

Today I looked at a lot of old pictures of myself from childhood. I saw the pre-social media me and the post social media me, and I could genuinely see that I was a lot happier before. I think ever since I got social media, I have been learning to perform a certain version of myself which is palatable / socially signals to people that I want to accept me. When I go through all my archives on instagram, I see this more clearly, and cringe at it. This past month I have worked a lot. I have lost a lot of conventionally success markers, I am tired, and my life wasn’t glamorous. I was trying, I was failing, and mostly I was trying to get up and try again. I realised yesterday night when I got back social media, that I do not know what my happiness looks like — when I don’t perform for anyone else. There are small things — like wearing nice clothes and reading on my bed, or listening to music and cooking. There is probably bigger things too, like laughing maniacally with my friends, and talking to relatives. Theres running around, and playing sports, and talking and talking. Those things cannot be shown as happiness. I sometimes refuse to believe that it all is.

Additionally, I find myself holding onto a version of me that fits this mysterious-sad vibe. It gives more gazey purpose to my life — creates a curiousity for the other person to care and all that. When I actually got to a place where I wasn’t happy, I couldnt do this performance of being sad. I dont even know what i was doing. that numbness is a blur. I wanted people to see me for it, but I didnt want them to see me for it, and try to fix it. I was the artist of my own misery, whether it came to optics, or friendship or anything. I often thought that the mystery audience would see how I was as a friend, and deem me to be uncool (how the books i read defined cool). I wasn’t chic, or aloof, or kind but soft. I am loud asf, and I yap too much, and I often interrupt the other person talking. And I know people who like me anyways. I often wonder why do they? There is so much that is so clunky, and selfish and imperfect about her. So hypocritical. but, they do anyways. like they actually do. I don’t really like myself a lot; kinda uncomfortable with the way all these different parts of me fit together. but other people, actually.. do like me. it is weird.

this brings me to the crux of this. I think I want to try to actually be happy. Theres a lot of fear in doing that. When someone clearly cares for me, I must engage in that fully. I must see it for all of it, and hold it even though the optics is not movie-esque or anything. I must push past the gaze and stop performing. I dont know if the words get through to how much resistance there is here. The coolest people have real lives with real love. I also do, but I never appreciate it enough in the intense everyday moment.

This also continues onto the way i live life. When I lived according to the prescription of someone else’s gaze, there was no doubt about why I took a decision (from small to big ones). The decision would signal something that I wanted it to signal to the people I wanted to signal to. But now, if I don’t care about what I signal, how do I want to live my life? It is scary, because there is no guarantee that the decisions I take are going to be good for me. and theres noone Im selling the polished version of my experience to. This goes for career, and romance and all of that.

its not possible to get rid of the gaze. but the gaze breathes down my neck all the time. And, tbh, my life is bigger than that. I don’t want to think about what anyone but I believe in when I have children eventually. or buy a home. its just, all confusing. since I dont really know a lot about myself.

but we will figure it out. eventually.

title: Designing systems to reason temporally: Looking at philosophy
subtitle: We stand on the shoulders of giants
html:
What does it mean for a system to understand time? We often treat this as a binary – either a system understands time or it does not. But this is a compression that exists in the vague, and doesn’t flesh out into the specifics. A particular creature could do the following

  1. Detect change, without having a persistent representation of an object

  2. Represent succession without having any understanding of causality

  3. Predict continuation, without considering other ways to think about the problem

  4. Imagine alternative ways of reasoning, without necessarily being able to organize actions into a plan.

I write this from reading an AI generated document, decomposing it only to what is important, and pushing further on what I find interesting. I will be looking at all of these ideas, and grounding them on how our world models (AI systems) are designed to handle these things. I hope this enriches my understanding of temporal reasoning (& understanding), in order to design systems that could suck less at temporal reasoning.

Bear in mind, this is the process of reading ideas, rather than coming up with a unified taxonomy or a golden definition of what temporal reasoning is. I am just doing the exercise of cruising through some philosophical ideas, and seeing if it can open up some useful abstractions. A lot of it, just was reading at the end. This article may, hence, contain a lot of noise. If you wish to skip the process of discovery, I recommend you to go to the conclusion.

In hindsight, as i kept reading, a loose structure started to emerge in how I was thinking about these problems. The questions broadly circle, these ideas

  1. What operations are our current systems trying to perform

  2. What information about the past and present must its representation preserve to make that operation possible

  3. At what level of abstraction and time scale should that information live

  4. How would the system know when its current representation is no longer sufficient?

Here is my messy process.

We start with the question – what makes time available to cognition at all? And then move to increasingly structured forms of reasoning. We look at current philosophy and literature.

We know that the perceptual stream of information is rich and approximately continuous, while the model sees discrete observation. What should a model represent for it to sufficiently speak about what persists, what changes, what causes what, and what could happen next; and what actions should be taken?

Temporal intelligence is a stack of competencies, rather than a single faculty.

Aristotle: time as a measure of change

(Time becomes intelligible through the distinction between before and after in motion, and through our capacity to count or measure that ordered change.)

A static description of a state can represent two different states independently. Temporal cognition begins when the two are not merely stored side by side but are represented as ordered phases of one changing process.

We can look at three increasingly structured notions

Difference -> ordered difference -> measured ordered difference

  • Something is different, the difference has a direction (one phase before another), third, the interval can be counted or compared.

Why numbers are important for time

The temporal actions before and after are grounded in motion. A moving object occupies different phases along a path. The ordering of those phases allow us to mark one as earlier and another as later. Time arises when the ordering can be articulated in terms of before and after. This is what makes a clock useful – it can be used to measure change as more or less, shorter or longer, earlier or later.

Assumption of persistence

When we say that a pedestrian moved from the curb into the road, cognition binds two appearances to one continuing entity. Without identity across observations, we have “person-like-pattern here” and “person-like-pattern there”. To identify that there is motion, there is a requirement of a relation between successive states of the same thing.

States recognized -> identity across states -> change -> before/after -> duration

Predicting the future from succession

Aristotle differentiates future-tense propositions from present tense once, since they are non deterministic. The question “what has happened” can be described as an ordered actuality. But, the question of “what can happen?” introduces a branching possibility. A temporal reasoner must be wary of treating the most likely continuation as though it is the only metaphysically available continuation.

In conclusion, what does Aristotle contribute to a hierarchy of temporal reasoning

  • Differentiate: World is not the same state

  • Bind: recognize successive states as phases of one entity or process

  • Order: represent one phase as before or after another

  • Measure: compare intervals, rates, or durations.

How to build a system that understands time; according to Aristotle.

Looking at this through the way we design our AI systems, we either take the most probable continuation or the top-x more probable continuations. But, a model does allow for the option of other available continuations; so there aren’t any contradictions of Aristotle’s ideas in current model design. We try to design our AI systems to gitsogood that it mimics/understands (in a rough sense) the assumptions we have about a video/temporal object; and do continuation accordingly. Till now, showing the model enough samples seems to achieve this, through a simulated-type-plasticity. It sees a “pattern” (say, a before after pattern, change, etc), and that can dissolve to a brief, repeated, approximate abstraction of the same idea – which can work as a way to understand “temporal properties” (atleast – of change, and a before and an after). Example: model sees ice melt enough, and then understands that ice was big block, now more curved, and; from its existing approximate internal model, it can predict that ice more curved. It doesn’t need to understand causality, or what ice is, or how it interacts with the environment. Functionally this is useful to detect change. Similarly, we know that our world models understand the property of persistence and continuity.

Our current systems can do object identification (identity). It can differentiate between two states, and bind that to a particular objects. Our models can understand and measure order.

Augustine: The present of Memory, Attention and Expectation

(Aka, how do we live in time?)

Not to be confused with this banger movie

The past no longer exists, the future does not yet exist, and the present has no duration. We still remember, attend, anticipate, compare intervals and recite temporally extended sequences. Augustine asks us to analyze temporal experience through a present memory of the past, present attention to what is occurring and present expectation of what is to come.

The current relation to the past comes in the form of memory. The future doesn’t need to exist for us to have a current relation to it, through expectation. The present attention is the mind’s active engagement with what is happing in the now.

A useful abstraction is:

Where M is what is retained as past, A is what is present attention, and E is an anticipated continuation; all at some given time instance t.

Distentio: the mind is stretched

Augustine calls temporal existence a distentio animi -> distention or stretching of the mind. The rough idea is this, we never experience the present as an isolated point. When we experience the present, part of what just happened is mentally available and a part of what is about to happen is already anticipated. Augustine calls this as the mind being stretched out across time. This stretching is what makes a sequence intelligible. The stretching is what allows us to notice change and ordering (from the previous section), and more abstract temporal patterns like a melody. To infer an action we need a temporal neighbourhood. To interpret the present, we would need to represent the recent past, the expectation of the future.

Reading augustine would suggest that temporal intelligence depends on atleast three things

  1. Compression of the past: not every previous input remains equally salient. The system may need sufficient memory for current interpretation.

  2. Selective attention to the present: Not every current feature matters equally

  3. Structured anticipation: prediction should be conditioned on both remembered trajectory and current evidence.

Augustine’s philosophy tells us how a subject can carry an ordered process through the present

Design of our AI systems, the food for thought, and a lot of thinking

The most blaring thing that this made me realise, is that our AI systems (in general, but especially our latent world models) treat perception and prediction as different problems. This made me go into a rabbithole on why this design structure is useful for AI systems. (bear this slight, but relevant tangent).

Most AI systems do not require expectation to exist as an explicit persistent object. We have historically optimized for representation to map a sufficient state and not explicit expectation. Ie, we want to find a h = f(x_past) that summarizes everything relevant about the past. The system makes decision using the representation h,:- like d = g(h). If h is sufficient enough of a representation, theoretically, we do not need to store expectation.

We can look further at our language models, and see that we do have predictive mechanisms, and a way to measure expectation. This can be explicit, to see which next-words have the highest probability, or the way world models can be evaluated on “suprise” (ie, a distance metric between the ground truth representation of the future, and the prediction ‘d’ of the future).

Adding on to this, what would training for expectation look like – a set of all future possibilities can explode. So, AI systems tend to collapse future understanding into one prediction, or a value. Expectation could also condition a model to continue the “most expected” state; which could hurt diversity of future possibilities. Expectation can bias & help interpretation.

Our current AI systems treat expectation like behaviour that a model can exhibit based on what it already knows (from its sufficient state) rather than something that is inbuilt into the system. Like a human separates expectation from an objective truth.

This gives me more clarity on some of the implicit design principles in our models. We want our models to

  1. be optimized for what we can measure (aka objective functions)

  2. learn the smallest sufficient representation

  3. Make representations differentiable and trainable (and try not to operate in an explosive search space)

  4. Scale & generalize

And we implicitly assume that a good prediction implies a good temporal representation. Our models are hence built on functional philosophy.

I think the difference in how we define a sufficient representation. I am following this thread of thought. Essentially, when we do not represent expectation, we aren’t giving the model mechanisms to “understand” surprise, rather, only exhibit surprise. Let’s probe into what sufficient can mean. This can be either of the following

  1. Statistical sufficiency: preserving everything relevant to the target. Here the question matters.

  2. Minimal sufficiency: preserving what matters and nothing else. This looks like compressing the past while retaining task relevant structure.

  3. Markov sufficiency: Preserve everything needed to continue the process. Representing everything about the past that matters for what happens next.

  4. Predictive sufficiency: Preserves the distributions of the future. Aka, the idea that a good temporal representation groups histories according to their possible futures

  5. Control sufficiency: preserve everything required to choose the right action

  6. Causal sufficiency: This is representation that encodes the causal structure -> ie, mechanisms, interventions, latent causes, which variable affects the other.

  7. Counterfactual sufficiency: a sufficient representation must retain enough information about the situation to construct an alternative world while preserving everything that should remain unchanged.

  8. Planning sufficiency: understanding current state, available actions constraints, future consequences. This is also goal relevant.

These are broad, lossy ways (pun unintended) to describe all the ways we can go about designing representations. What does representing surprise give us?

  1. In a technical level: prediction error, probabilistic suprise (rare events surprise the model), bayesian surprise (how much does observing an event force you to revise a model).

  2. On a meta level:

    1. surprise tells your model (ie, as a part of its “representation”) whether its representation is sufficient for the observations it received.

    2. It can allow us to refine our representations by giving a signal to the model that it failed to encode something.

    3. Surprise can tell you where to allocate your attention.

    4. Surprise can create event boundaries (aka something new happened) & reveal hidden causes

The gist of it is that surprise lets us distinguish knowing an event from understanding its place in a process. Parts of meta-learning basically look like this. Based on the prediction, we get error/suprise, which helps update our representations.

In a temporal setting, surprise touches our fast brain (if we assume that the brain has a fast and slow mechanism of processing). If a model understands expectation, and is “let down” for its expectation, should it change its representation of the event hypothesis? Of the object state? A causal hypothesis? Is expectation functionally useful for intelligence? Yes, if we gain a lot from using prediction to structure our perception. These ideas are explored more in predictive coding.

To conclude, expectation when it comes to temporal reasoning, allows the model a better avenue to represent its own understanding of directionality.

Bratman: Intention as a structure for planning through time

(From possible futures to committed, hierarchical action)

Michael Bratman argues that intentions can acts as planning states that stabilize future actions, constrain late deliberation, support means-end reasoning and enable coordination across time. Plans are typically partial and become more specific as action approaches.

Now, what is intention according to this understanding? -> It is a decision that you temporarily treat as settled. The intention to attend a conference, for example, would lead you to plan about booking a flight, organizing transport, etc. Your intention influences your future decisions. Here, it is almost treated as committing to an idea/future state, and organizing local future states accordingly.

Bratman talks about the importance in intention when it comes to temporal planning. When we consider future actions, one can consider all possible future actions. Intention here, has a stabilizing role – as a decision process would consume less resources with it.

Deliberation -> intention -> constrained later deliberation.

Additionally, most human plans exist in the vague (ie, not fully specific). You are more likely to hear someone say that they want to “get rich in the future” instead of their exact steps to get there. That vague intention, can later lead to constrained deliberation on specifics.

A planning agent fundamentally has to look at multiple future trajectories, and have a mechanism to be able to give us the “what the setup will do” as a desirable state, i.e. with high probability.

This way of dividing one big vague intention, and organizing future subgoals, into subplans, and taking action accordingly – leads to a hierarchy of reasoning. These different abstractions corresponds to different time scales.

Example: the broad intention to drive safely, may last 30 minutes in the midst of driving. Yields to pedestrians on the road may last 30 seconds, and the specific use of using an accelerator or a decelerator becomes a 1 second decision. We see that higher abstractions can be mapped to larger time scales, while lower abstractions can be mapped to smaller timescales.

This intention maps the way one goes about temporal reasoning. An agent which can “voice out” what it wants to/ought to do has the ability to plan hierarchically & reason about the means to a particular end. This acts effectively as a form of temporal compression; because you use intention to reduce your search space of possible future states / possible understandings of the present states.

Now planning as we have defined it is very static. We need our planning agent to also receive new stimulus and replan / keep plan; ie reasoning about whether to reason again (meta reasoning)

This way of thinking would assume that planning can be broken down to -> counterfactual reasoning + commitment.

Look at possible futures -> find action conditioned futures -> evaluate -> choose -> commit. An agent that can temporarily reason to the highest sense, needs to be able to organizationally commit continuously. This commitment should act as an intent, and drive multiple scales of reasoning -> which can be understanding change, temporal rules, etc.

Conclusion: What does it mean then, to reason temporally?

Let us make the premise clearer. I started with the broad question of “how do our systems understand time?”. My implicit goal in that process was to ask, how does a system process and utilize a temporal sequence; and more so, what should we find as important when we are designing systems to temporally reason. A lot of current literature (Tempcompass, PerceptionTest, Clevrer, and more) define temporal reasoning really vaguely. So I looked at what the philosophers thought about reasoning temporally; and understanding time.

We start with Aristotle, who tells us how we can abstractly look at time: ie, through a before and after in an ordering with an assumption of persistence & identity of an object, and with the property of predicting some sort of succession.

Then Augustine (and Husserl*), tells us how we process and practically live in time – our every temporal event is associated with a past, a present (in a memory) and a future (through expectation); which we all use to understand the present, and “think” about a future. I here went on a deep dive on what matters in our AI systems when they “understand” time. I use the word understand, as the word represents/ or perceive. We look at 1) What matters in a representation and 2. What is a temporally sufficient representation?

Then, finally I look at Bratman, who looks at what temporal reasoning look like, and how we could think about hierarchies in temporal reasoning. We see that higher abstractions of “reasoning” (aka, planning) depends on our ability to counterfactually reason, along with being able to commit to a direction in the possible trajectories of actions (which he calls intention).

Additional discourse (which I add below), discusses how we can think about temporal reasoning logically (Prior), how is causality different from prediction (Kant), and what comes from discretizing a continuous signal like a temporal signal (Bergson). A summary of those perspectives are in the next section, for your perusal.

Ultimately, this all adds formalized perspective towards how to think about problems. I am curious, to see how our current systems are actually designed (beyond what I have already read). Some other questions I find interesting

  1. Do we need language to shape intention/ design a plan to commit; which could lead to a hierarchical way of thinking?

  2. What are the various ways we are designing systems to look at temporal reasoning

  3. What does seeing the presence or absence of particular rules give us for temporal reasoning? What does industry care about with the way the build models.

I am curious too, to hear what others think :D

.

.

.

.

.

.

.

.

.

.

.

.

.

.

Some bonus ideas that add interesting perspective

Which are additive, rather than necessarily multiplicative.

Arthur Prior: Temporal Reasoning becomes logic

(From temporal representations to propositions about past and future.)

From representations to temporally qualified claims

All the work till now asks how temporal structure is either perceived or constituted. Prior asks what happens when temporal structure enters logic. Lets take a statement p = ‘the pedestrian is in the road’. The truth of p may change. It can be false, then true and later false. Classical propositional logic itself doesn’t encode temporal variation. Tense logic can replace dates, but adding operations like this

Pp: it was the case that p

Fp: it will be the case that p

(Standard developments also use operations corresponding to “always in the past” and “always in the future”)

Now, temporal questions become formal relations among propositions.

p -> Fq; can express that if p is true now, then q will be true at some later time. We can always add more rules to see things like eventually, always until, bounded time, and branching alternatives.

These operations are different from dates, because it gives a language for relationships that remain meaningful across different absolute dates. This kind of formulation helps us generalize to more complex relations.

Some of the cool things tense logic can do

  • Tense logic exposes compositional structure

    • FFp -> there will be a future point from which p is still future

  • The future can branch

    • From one pedestrian state, many futures can emerge. We can find these branches to be future trajectories.

  • More complex, but we could allow for counterfactuals to get set up

The biggest contribution to understanding temporal reasoning was giving it a language for evaluation. We could ask relational questions about states which spans causality, continuity, etc.

Kant: what can we say about causality

Kant says that we can split temporal understanding into levels

  1. What did the ego object observe first

  2. What actually happened first

  3. Did the events of earlier cause or constrain the later ones?

A temporal model hence, needs to understand what persists, what changes, what coexists, and what causes what.

Husserl: Retention, Impression, Protention

(How a sequence becomes one temporally extended object)

Husserl’s analysis of internal time consciousness asks how we can directly experience a temporally extended object – something like a melody, movement or a sentence, rather than a sequence of disconnected instantaneous contents.

Let’s take a melody. If we play Sa, Re, Ga; when Ga plays we do not hear Sa anymore. It is no longer present acoustically. Yet, if Sa vanished from our understanding, we would not recognize the sequence as a melody. He defines the representation of an experience at time t as:

Where I is the primal impression: the narrowly current phase, R is the retention: just past, and P is the protention; which is the horizon of what is about to occur. Together, they make a current note as a phase of a motion.

Husserl further says that our retention can be recursive. The idea is that something in my immediate past itself depends on things from its immediate past. The broad idea is that temporal position is encoded relationally. We can see ideas like multiscale memory or state space representation in which temporal distance changes how information is represented.

Protention here is very similar to Expectation for Augustine’s understanding of time. The difference in Husserl’s understanding is that retention and protention is a subset of memory / expectation. It operates in the microstructure of ongoing experience.

Bergson: Duration before Discretization

(What do we lose when we represent continuous becoming into discrete states?)

When we are listening to a musical sequence, each note in the future changes the significance of the notes that came before. Similarly, a pedestrian may gradually lean forward, shift their weight, and begin to step. A frame based representation may label the states as ‘standing, standing, walking’. But Bergson argues that the transition may matter before any categorical boundary is crossed. The body already becomes a walking body; and a system that only recognizes the label change after a threshold, may miss information present in the continuous deformation. This idea is cool, but doesn’t practically add a lot when we are trying to find minimal viable good representations to functionally help us temporally reason better.

But, fundamentally, it reminds us what we should care about when we are building models that help us represent and understand time. Our LLMs can tell us things like our writing makes it “feel” something, but that is functional larping about something which is inherit to our human consciousness (maybe :p that’s not a conversation im starting). At the end of the day, temporal reasoning models do not need to appreciate music, but it should be able to reason about patterns.

Before i piss off the consciousness bros

title: दिन ये गुजारूँ कैसे, इतना बता जा?
subtitle: asar, muslim shaggan
html:
.

.

i will use sharp words to speak my love, sharper than the poems that yearn for you.

the force of our words was a lattice to the warmth i held for you.

the senses were never confused. they would follow you everywhere.

the heart knew how to rest.

i found my voice with you. i spoke my world loudly, then softly, the in trembles to you. to the you shaped walls, and ceilings.

these songs roll around my tongue. they make my body tremble like the winter i knew i lost you forever.

.

this ggreif, retches, out of my cold lifeless body

.

noone will ever see this love I have for you. Only I will.

Isn’t that so lonely?

.

this will wrap its tendrils around itself, and fall out like tears.

.

you are a part of my sensory life. all my cells have changed since then. but my mind knows. so, how can I not love you forever?

.

_____*, i sometimes wonder whether the depth in my life came in because I grew up, or because I grew up with you.

i think i will never know.

.

your eyes were enough to hold this grief.

.

असर उसको ज़रा नहीं होता।
तुम हमारे किसी तरह न हुए,
वरना दुनिया में क्या नहीं होता!

*redacted in post processing

title: The woes in between
subtitle: fiction
html:
9:34pm.

We were out for drinks. The lights were dim and you called my cigarette one with a lot of personality. I said that a friend got me onto it. I could barely hear you, and the music was too quiet, so we went to a place louder.

9:47pm.

The DJ was an old man, much like a father, and we were confused. The people around us are shaking their heads to the music, shaking their bodies listlessly. The wind is cool, and the music rises. I’m sorry, I can’t hear you. Yeah, I will come closer.

10:01pm

Lets play a game, the weird in between of a new conversation. I overshare. I say so much that nothing goes through. You now know the events of my life. I am now ashamed. I may as well now be a typecast in your head.

11:12pm

Ah the drudgery. Ah the shame. And ugh, the bile in my throat.

12:04am

The ceiling shows us something distinct. My sprawled out body, the echo of the words in my head. the quiet that stayed unsaid. the quiet that fills this room and bounces off the warm lighting. the ringing in my ears. I don’t really know how to be myself. The fan above me spins, and

5:07am

Where am I? Ughhhh why is the light on?

Ughhhhhh my body hurts.

2 days later, 4:50 am.

I am caught in the woes in between. I really love this old full sleeve t-shirt. It makes me feel small, as its sleeves stretches out past my finger tips. The hems on the shoulders fall low. It smells like home. It fits on me different. It doesn’t really work for office.
Ah. Office. I have that tomorrow, well in 4 hours actually.

This new city is like a sequin top. This new city is like the crisp crinkle of a formal cotton. I wear it to be an adult. I straighten out all the places my iron didn’t catch. I frown at myself.

I spent an hour looking at what all my friends are doing. Their medallion of a career. their linkedin formal smiles. I haven’t seen these people since high school. I, remember them being warm, and kind. It has been long since I have been a high school kid. I had my own little world then. In this noggin.

.

what was the future back then? it was a rhetoric question that was pretentious to answer. Do I look like I have it all figured out. I remember liking my primary school slides. and the nets I used to climb. And I used to walk around for hours, listening to Blur, and Muse, and Radiohead in the end of high school. what was future then? the thing I worked so hard for? Why did I work so hard? why did I work at all. there is work tomorrow-ugh

.

.

there was a time when grass felt crisp, the way an adjective that hasn’t met a formal tshirt feels. The wind caught at me as I ran.

there was a time before the void of love. there is a time after?

the elusive f u t u r e

.

all i know is, I hate that I have to plan. I hate being responsible and ambitious. I want to merge with the couch and read. I want to go to school and tell my best friend who I love the stories I read. I want and want and want

i don’t want to strap myself to a tomorrow where the disappointment of a world hits

i want to speak to someone and be heard like a hug

and ALL those other poetic repetitions of a want

.

this little world of mine.

I dont ask you to care,

but oh dear, will you please?
